passages.text: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice.
passages.sermon:
A king will rule.
This king will act with righteousness.
Princes will govern.
These princes will use justice.
passages.original: הֵ֥ן לְצֶ֖דֶק יִמְלָךְ־ מֶ֑לֶךְ וּלְשָׂרִ֖ים לְמִשְׁפָּ֥ט יָשֹֽׂרוּ׃

passages.text: Each will be like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in an arid land.
passages.sermon:
A righteous king will reign.
His princes will rule with justice.
Each ruler will protect the people.
He will be like a shelter from the wind.
He will be a refuge from the storm.
He will be like streams of water in a dry land.
He will be like the shadow of a great rock in an arid land.
passages.original: וְהָיָה־ אִ֥ישׁ כְּמַֽחֲבֵא־ ר֖וּחַ וְסֵ֣תֶר זָ֑רֶם כְּפַלְגֵי־ מַ֣יִם בְּצָי֔וֹן כְּצֵ֥ל סֶֽלַע־ כָּבֵ֖ד בְּאֶ֥רֶץ עֲיֵפָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
passages.sermon:
People will see clearly.
Their eyes will not be closed.
People who hear will pay attention.
Their ears will listen.
passages.original: וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁעֶ֖ינָה עֵינֵ֣י רֹאִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י שֹׁמְעִ֖ים תִּקְשַֽׁבְנָה׃

passages.text: The mind of the rash will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will speak clearly and fluently.
passages.sermon:
God will change people.
He will help those who act quickly and without thinking.
Their minds will know.
Their minds will understand.
God will help those who cannot speak well.
Their tongues will speak quickly.
Their words will be clear.
Their speech will be easy to understand.
passages.original: וּלְבַ֥ב נִמְהָרִ֖ים יָבִ֣ין לָדָ֑עַת וּלְשׁ֣וֹן עִלְּגִ֔ים תְּמַהֵ֖ר לְדַבֵּ֥ר צָחֽוֹת׃

passages.text: No longer will a fool be called noble, nor a scoundrel be respected.
passages.sermon:
A fool is a person who acts without wisdom or respect for God.
A scoundrel is a person who does evil and harms others.
People will not call a fool noble anymore.
People will not call a scoundrel honorable anymore.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יִקָּרֵ֥א ע֛וֹד לְנָבָ֖ל נָדִ֑יב וּלְכִילַ֕י לֹ֥א יֵֽאָמֵ֖ר שֽׁוֹעַ׃

passages.text: For a fool speaks foolishness; his mind plots iniquity. He practices ungodliness and speaks falsely about the LORD; he leaves the hungry empty and deprives the thirsty of drink.
passages.sermon:
A fool speaks foolish words.
A fool’s mind plans evil.
A fool does ungodly things.
A fool tells lies about the LORD.
A fool leaves hungry people with nothing.
A fool does not give drink to the thirsty.
passages.original: כִּ֤י נָבָל֙ נְבָלָ֣ה יְדַבֵּ֔ר וְלִבּ֖וֹ יַעֲשֶׂה־ אָ֑וֶן לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת חֹ֗נֶף וּלְדַבֵּ֤ר אֶל־ יְהוָה֙ תּוֹעָ֔ה לְהָרִיק֙ נֶ֣פֶשׁ רָעֵ֔ב וּמַשְׁקֶ֥ה צָמֵ֖א יַחְסִֽיר׃

passages.text: The weapons of the scoundrel are destructive; he hatches plots to destroy the poor with lies, even when the plea of the needy is just.
passages.sermon:
A scoundrel uses evil tools.
He makes plans to harm others.
He tries to destroy poor people with lies.
He speaks falsely against the needy.
He does this even when the needy ask for justice.
passages.original: וְכֵלַ֖י כֵּלָ֣יו רָעִ֑ים ה֚וּא זִמּ֣וֹת יָעָ֔ץ לְחַבֵּ֤ל עֲנָוִים בְּאִמְרֵי־ שֶׁ֔קֶר וּבְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶבְי֖וֹן מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

passages.text: But a noble man makes honorable plans; he stands up for worthy causes.
passages.sermon:
A noble man acts with honor.
He makes good and generous plans.
He stands up for what is right.
He supports worthy causes.
passages.original: וְנָדִ֖יב נְדִיב֣וֹת יָעָ֑ץ וְה֖וּא עַל־ נְדִיב֥וֹת יָקֽוּם׃פ

passages.text: Stand up, you complacent women; listen to me. Give ear to my word, you overconfident daughters.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah speaks to the women of Jerusalem.
These women feel secure and at ease.
Isaiah calls them complacent and overconfident.
He commands these women to stand up.
He tells them to listen to his voice.
He urges the daughters who trust in themselves to pay attention to his words.
passages.original: נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י בָּנוֹת֙ בֹּֽטח֔וֹת הַאְזֵ֖נָּה אִמְרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: In a little more than a year you will tremble, O secure ones. For the grape harvest will fail and the fruit harvest will not arrive.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to women who feel secure and confident.
He warns them about the future.
In a little more than a year, you will tremble.
You feel safe now.
But soon, you will be afraid.
The grape harvest will fail.
No fruit will be gathered.
The harvest will not come.
passages.original: יָמִים֙ עַל־ שָׁנָ֔ה תִּרְגַּ֖זְנָה בֹּֽטְח֑וֹת כִּ֚י כָּלָ֣ה בָצִ֔יר אֹ֖סֶף בְּלִ֥י יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Shudder, you ladies of leisure; tremble, you daughters of complacency. Strip yourselves bare and put sackcloth around your waists.
passages.sermon:
Isaiah speaks to women who feel safe and comfortable.
These women live in ease and do not worry.
Isaiah calls them "ladies of leisure" and "daughters of complacency."
He tells them to shudder and tremble.
He commands them to strip off their fine clothes.
He tells them to put sackcloth around their waists.
passages.original: חִרְדוּ֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת רְגָ֖זָה בֹּֽטְח֑וֹת פְּשֹׁ֣טָֽה וְעֹ֔רָה וַחֲג֖וֹרָה עַל־ חֲלָצָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines, and for the land of my people, overgrown with thorns and briers— even for every house of merriment in this city of revelry.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He warns them about coming judgment.
He tells them to mourn.
He says, "Beat your breasts."
He tells them to grieve for the pleasant fields.
He tells them to grieve for the fruitful vines.
He says the land of God's people will be covered with thorns and briers.
He says every house of joy in the city will be affected.
He says even the city of celebration will face sorrow.
passages.original: עַל־ שָׁדַ֖יִם סֹֽפְדִ֑ים עַל־ שְׂדֵי־ חֶ֕מֶד עַל־ גֶּ֖פֶן פֹּרִיָּֽה׃ עַ֚ל אַדְמַ֣ת עַמִּ֔י ק֥וֹץ שָׁמִ֖יר תַּֽעֲלֶ֑ה כִּ֚י עַל־ כָּל־ בָּתֵּ֣י מָשׂ֔וֹשׂ קִרְיָ֖ה עַלִּיזָֽה׃

passages.text: For the palace will be forsaken, the busy city abandoned. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever— the delight of wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks— until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the desert will be an orchard, and the orchard will seem like a forest.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
The palace will be empty.
People will leave the busy city.
The hill and the watchtower will become empty places.
These places will turn into caves.
Wild donkeys will find joy there.
Flocks will eat there.
This will last for a long time.
It will continue until God pours out His Spirit from above.
When God sends His Spirit, the desert will change.
The desert will become like an orchard.
The orchard will become like a forest.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַרְמ֣וֹן נֻטָּ֔שׁ הֲמ֥וֹן עִ֖יר עֻזָּ֑ב עֹ֣פֶל וָבַ֜חַן הָיָ֨ה בְעַ֤ד מְעָרוֹת֙ עַד־ עוֹלָ֔ם מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ פְּרָאִ֖ים מִרְעֵ֥ה עֲדָרִֽים׃ עַד־ יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה עָלֵ֛ינוּ ר֖וּחַ מִמָּר֑וֹם וְהָיָ֤ה מִדְבָּר֙ לַכַּרְמֶ֔ל וְכַרְמֶל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: Then justice will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field.
passages.sermon: Justice will live in the wilderness.\r\nRighteousness will stay in the fertile field.
passages.original: וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בַּכַּרְמֶ֥ל תֵּשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: The work of righteousness will be peace; the service of righteousness will be quiet confidence forever.
passages.sermon:
Righteousness produces peace.
Righteousness brings quietness.
Righteousness gives confidence.
This peace, quietness, and confidence will last forever.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֛ה מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה הַצְּדָקָ֖ה שָׁל֑וֹם וַֽעֲבֹדַת֙ הַצְּדָקָ֔ה הַשְׁקֵ֥ט וָבֶ֖טַח עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
passages.sermon:
God’s people will live in peace.
They will stay in places that are safe.
They will rest in places that are secure.
They will have calm and quiet lives.
passages.original: וְיָשַׁ֥ב עַמִּ֖י בִּנְוֵ֣ה שָׁל֑וֹם וּֽבְמִשְׁכְּנוֹת֙ מִבְטַחִ֔ים וּבִמְנוּחֹ֖ת שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: But hail will level the forest, and the city will sink to the depths.
passages.sermon:
Hail will fall.
Hail will strike the forest.
Hail will flatten the forest.
The city will become low.
The city will sink down to the depths.
passages.original: וּבָרַ֖ד בְּרֶ֣דֶת הַיָּ֑עַר וּבַשִּׁפְלָ֖ה תִּשְׁפַּ֥ל הָעִֽיר׃

passages.text: Blessed are those who sow beside abundant waters, who let the ox and donkey range freely.
passages.sermon:
God blesses people who plant seeds by every stream.
These people work where there is plenty of water.
They let their oxen walk freely.
They let their donkeys walk freely.
God gives happiness to these people.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם זֹרְעֵ֖י עַל־ כָּל־ מָ֑יִם מְשַׁלְּחֵ֥י רֶֽגֶל־ הַשּׁ֖וֹר וְהַחֲמֽוֹר׃ס
